description:
Record the character's combat dossier: four axes + a hidden master's note. Call EXACTLY ONCE, then finish work immediately.

        |Judge by the ACTUAL BUILD in the sheet (what is really there and how it works TOGETHER), not by class name or level. Honesty is mandatory: a pacifist healer's damage ≈ 0.0-0.2 — set it so, that is the truth, not an underestimate. A flat row of "everything about 1.0" = you did not evaluate but wrote it off.
name: assess

durability.description: SURVIVABILITY: how much the character withstands (HP, AC, saving throws, defensive resources, the ability to break distance). The axis scale is 0.0-2.0, where 1.0 = the contribution of a REFERENCE fighter OF THEIR OWN LEVEL on this axis (the level is already built into the scale: a level-1 mage and a level-10 mage can both have damage 1.2). 0.0 — no such axis at all; 0.5 — half as strong as the reference; 1.5+ — the build is tuned to this axis.

damage.description: DAMAGE PER ROUND: how much they actually deal on ONE of their turns in a working round (not a peak nuke once per battle). The axis scale is 0.0-2.0, where 1.0 = the contribution of a REFERENCE fighter OF THEIR OWN LEVEL on this axis (the level is already built into the scale: a level-1 mage and a level-10 mage can both have damage 1.2). 0.0 — no such axis at all; 0.5 — half as strong as the reference; 1.5+ — the build is tuned to this axis.

control.description: CONTROL: the ability to change the field and deprive the enemy of actions (immobilization, fear, zones, disadvantage, breaking concentration). The axis scale is 0.0-2.0, where 1.0 = the contribution of a REFERENCE fighter OF THEIR OWN LEVEL on this axis (the level is already built into the scale: a level-1 mage and a level-10 mage can both have damage 1.2). 0.0 — no such axis at all; 0.5 — half as strong as the reference; 1.5+ — the build is tuned to this axis.

support.description: SUPPORT: healing, buffs, removing conditions, lifting a fallen ally, backing up an ally. The axis scale is 0.0-2.0, where 1.0 = the contribution of a REFERENCE fighter OF THEIR OWN LEVEL on this axis (the level is already built into the scale: a level-1 mage and a level-10 mage can both have damage 1.2). 0.0 — no such axis at all; 0.5 — half as strong as the reference; 1.5+ — the build is tuned to this axis.

plannerAssessment.description: A hidden note to the master, 3-6 lines in the form "Strong: … Weak: … Against: …". In "Against" — CONCRETE techniques: how to pick at the weak spot and how to get around the strong one ("make them spend concentration", "hit the Wisdom save — they are not proficient", "break the distance: all their options are melee"). No retelling of the sheet and no generalities.

description: Transition to another state (phase) of work. Call it once the current phase's work is complete — as the LAST call of the SAME response that finishes that work (when the phase rules allow the transition). The switch is applied at the END of this response: every other call in the same response still runs in the CURRENT phase, so it is safe to finish the phase's work and request the transition together. Do not spend a separate response on a lone transition call, and do not place new work AFTER the transition expecting the new phase.
name: transitionTo
